claim: Let \(C_n^k\) be the \(k\)-th power of the cycle on \(\mathbb Z_n\). For every noncomplete Dirac cycle power, equivalently \(\lceil n/4\rceil\le k<\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), one has \(\operatorname{rc}(C_n^k)=\operatorname{src}(C_n^k)=2\). If \(n<4k\), a generator-based two-coloring exists: color the edges of cyclic distance \(k\) red and all shorter generator edges blue. At the exact boundary \(n=4k\), no two-coloring depending only on cyclic distance can be rainbow connecting, but the following non-generator-based coloring is strongly rainbow connecting: write each edge uniquely as \(\{i,i+r\}\) with \(1\le r\le k\) modulo \(4k\), and color it by the parity of \(\lfloor i/k\rfloor\). Complete cycle powers have \(\operatorname{rc}=\operatorname{src}=1\).

correctness.rationale: For n<4k, every nonadjacent pair at cyclic distance d with k<d<=floor(n/2)<2k has the explicit geodesic u,u+k,v whose edge distances are k and d-k, hence opposite colors. For n=4k, the block-parity coloring makes the two starts u and u+k lie in blocks of opposite parity. The generator obstruction is exact because 0 and 2k have only common neighbors k and 3k, and both incident distances are k. Noncompleteness supplies the lower bound two. The standalone verifier stress-tests 312398 constructed nonadjacent pairs and independently brute-forces 5850 small-case pairs.
correctness.risks: The computation is finite and is not used as an infinite proof. The proof assumes the standard simple undirected cycle-power convention and the stated symmetric definition of generator-based coloring.

value.rationale: The result directly resolves the canonical family singled out in the new Dirac-circulant open problem. It explains the exact boundary where the natural generator-distance strategy fails while showing that rainbow connection itself still succeeds, and it strengthens ordinary rainbow connection to strong rainbow connection. This is a structural, infinite-family answer rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
value.risks: It is a subclass result and does not settle arbitrary circulants or Cayley graphs. Its value is primarily as a sharp model family and obstruction/construction pair for the broader question.
